# Command line

Prove small programs correct, and hold implementations to their specs. Every command `vector` declares, read from its declaration in [src/main.ts](https://github.com/amritk/vector/blob/main/src/main.ts) and the files it registers.

## Usage

```text
vector <command> [flags]
vector -v, --version | -h, --help
```

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`vector verify`](command-line/verify.md) | Prove a program meets its spec plan |
| [`vector diff`](command-line/diff.md) | Prove two programs equivalent, or show where they differ |
| `vector spec` | Turn a spec into a contract and a test, and gate changes on it |
| [`vector spec extract`](command-line/spec-extract.md) | Extract a contract from a kramdown-rfc spec's XML |
| [`vector spec check`](command-line/spec-check.md) | Check a contract's quotes and vectors against its source |
| [`vector spec emit`](command-line/spec-emit.md) | Emit the Nish test a contract implies |
| [`vector spec run`](command-line/spec-run.md) | Emit a contract's Nish test and run it |
| [`vector spec frozen`](command-line/spec-frozen.md) | Refuse a change that edits a frozen contract |
| [`vector spec stale`](command-line/spec-stale.md) | Refuse a generated test that no longer matches its contract |
| [`vector spec exports`](command-line/spec-exports.md) | Refuse a new export its contract does not cover |
| [`vector spec mutate`](command-line/spec-mutate.md) | Mutate the changed lines and refuse mutants the test misses |

## Global flags

<scalar-field name="-h, --help">

Show the help of the command it follows, and exit 0.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="-v, --version">

Print `vector`'s version, and exit 0.

</scalar-field>

## Exit codes

Every command ends with one of these, declared in [src/core/diag.ts](https://github.com/amritk/vector/blob/main/src/core/diag.ts).

| Code | Constant | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `EXIT_PASS` | The check ran and passed. |
| 1 | `EXIT_REFUSED` | The check ran and refused the input. |
| 2 | `EXIT_USAGE` | The command could not run: bad usage, or an I/O or tool failure. |
